notes: Weapon types, armour pieces and gear families are name-based where the wiki has no category (there are no Sword/Scimitar/... categories). Weapon type tags require 'Equipable items', so unstrung bows, tips and unfinished ammo are left to the fletching/smithing domains; ammo kind tags (arrow, bolt, javelin) likewise cover finished ammo only. Weapon types sit under their combat style (bow under ranged-weapon, staff under magic-weapon), so a type implies the style; stab/slash/crush come straight from the wiki attack-type categories. Salamander tars carry weapon categories on the wiki and are excluded from weapon tags. Metal tiers and gem families use the wiki's material categories, so they also cover ores, bars, uncut gems and bolt tips (shared with the smithing/crafting domains; keys follow the README). The 'dragon' tier uses the wiki category 'Orikalkum' (the wiki's current name for dragon metal) plus name rules; the 'Rune' category's cosmetic dragonstone armour is excluded. 'white' = White Knight equipment. Dragonhide colour tags include leather and hides so the crafting chain shares a colour. God tags are name-based and include god pages, hilts, ornament kits and sets, excluding potions. boss-drop/raid-unique use the boss and raid wiki categories minus potions and teleports, so they include non-equipment uniques (jars, sigils, contracts, Huasca seed). item-set sits under misc because it also holds potion and page sets. The shared roots (equipment, weapon, armour, jewellery, ammunition, material, source, misc) are repeated here so the tree validates on its own. Unresolved: cosmetic clothing, tiaras, blessings and holy symbols are left to the misc/prayer/runecraft domains and only get slot tags here; whips, scythes and ballistae (1-2 GE items each) have no type tag of their own.
